chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said:

I saw Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) in the year two hundred and twenty-five, bidding farewell to the House after the sun had risen, and performing Tawaf of the House, touching the Yamani Corner during each circuit. So when it was the seventh circuit, he touched it and touched the Stone, and wiped with his hand, then wiped his face with his hand.

Then he went to the Maqam (Standing Place of Ibrahim), so he performed two cycles of Salat behind it. Then he went out to the back of the Ka'bah, to the Multazam, so he adhered to the House, and uncovered the cloth from his belly, then paused upon it for a long time, supplicating. Then he went out from the door of al-Hannatayn and faced it.

He said, So I also saw him in the year two hundred and seventeen bidding farewell to the House at night, touching the Yamani Corner and the Black Stone during each circuit. So when he was in the seventh circuit, he adhered to the House at the back of the Ka'bah, near to the Yamani Corner, and above the elongated Stone, and uncovered the cloth from his belly. Then he went to the Stone, so he kissed it, and wiped it, and went to the Maqam, so he performed Salat behind it. Then he went and did not return to the House.
And his pausing at the Multazam was of a measurement of what some of our companions take to perform Tawaf of seven circuits, and some of them eight.

key_terms.الرُّكْنُ الْيَمَانِي: The Yamani Corner of the Ka'bah, touched during Tawaf
key_terms.الْمَقَام: The Standing Place of Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْمُلْتَزَم: The section of the Ka'bah wall between the door and the Yamani Corner, where pilgrims adhere to supplicate

ai.seo_question: What are the specific ritual steps for bidding farewell to the Ka'bah according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the ritual significance of 'Tadi' (bidding farewell) to the Ka'bah, a practice emphasized in Shia jurisprudence to conclude the pilgrimage with heightened devotion. It details Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) specific actions, such as touching the Yamani Corner and Black Stone during every circuit and the final supplication at the Multazam, illustrating the integration of physical acts with spiritual reflection. This narration serves as a primary source for the recommended etiquette of concluding Hajj or Umrah, reinforcing the connection between the pilgrim and the Divine House.
